title: Editor placeholder uses a JSX string-literal attribute, so backslash-n renders as literal "\n" instead of newlines
description:
The placeholder is written as a JSX double-quoted attribute: `placeholder="# Write reusable helper functions here

import polars as pl

def my_helper(df):
    return df"`. JSX string-literal attribute values (single/double quotes) are parsed like HTML attribute text and do NOT process backslash escape sequences, so the four `
` sequences are passed verbatim. CodeMirror's placeholder() then renders the literal characters `
` on a single line rather than line breaks, producing a garbled hint. Sibling editors deliberately use the JS-expression brace form so escapes are processed: ImportsPanel.tsx:35 `placeholder={"from utility.features import *
import numpy as np
..."}` and DataSourceEditor.tsx:99 `placeholder={"SELECT *
FROM ..."}`. This file should use `placeholder={"...
..."}` for the newlines to take effect.
evidence:
Line 266: `placeholder="# Write reusable helper functions here

import polars as pl

def my_helper(df):
    return df"` (no braces). Contrast ImportsPanel.tsx:35 and DataSourceEditor.tsx:99 which wrap the multi-line string in `{}`. The mock in UtilityPanel.test.tsx:12 forwards `placeholder` to a real textarea but no test asserts its content, so the defect is uncaught.
